al1.title: Light the Lights
al1.story: Your Altair kit is finally soldered together. Time to make the lights do something.
al1.task: Write a program that makes the lights show the pattern 10100101, then stops. One byte per line: MVI A, the pattern, OUT, 377, HLT.
hints: MVI A is 00 111 110.
The value is just the pattern: 10 100 101.

al2.title: The Adding Machine
al2.story: The Altair as a pocket calculator: it can only add one byte, but it adds it fast.
al2.task: Make the Altair work out 100 + 55 and show it, then 200 + 100 and show that too (watch it overflow). Use MVI A and ADI (11 000 110) for both sums.
hints: The second sum the same way: 200 is 11 001 000, 100 is 01 100 100.

al3.title: Octal Only
al3.story: A friend sends you a program printed in octal, the way magazines did. Now write one yourself.
al3.task: Write a program in octal only (3 digits per line) that shows octal 125 on the lights, then octal 252, then stops.

requirements.message: Write the bytes in octal, like 076.

hints: MVI A is 076, OUT is 323, the lights are 377, HLT is 166.
076, 125, 323, 377 shows the first pattern.

alc1-project.title: The Light Show
alc1-project.story: Altair owners loved to show off their machine to friends with blinking light patterns.
alc1-project.task: Show these five patterns on the lights, one after the other: 10000001, 01000010, 00100100, 00011000, 11111111. Then stop.
hints: Each pattern needs four bytes: MVI A, the pattern, OUT, 377.
Five times, then 01 110 110 (HLT): 21 bytes in all.

al4.title: Register Shuffle
al4.story: The registers are like seven little boxes on your desk. Shuffle the values around.
al4.task:
Put 1 into B and 2 into C with MVI. Swap B and C using another register as the parking spot (not A), then show B on the lights, then C:
LEDS ○○○○○○●○ = 2
LEDS ○○○○○○○● = 1

requirements.message: Use MOV to copy between registers.

hints: Swap with D: MOV D,B (120), MOV B,C (101), MOV C,D (112).
Show B: MOV A,B (170), OUT 377 (323 377). Then MOV A,C (171), OUT 377, HLT.

al5.title: Times Ten
al5.story: Your Altair needs to multiply by 10 a lot. Find a fast way without a loop.
al5.task:
Load 13 into A. Multiply it by 10 using only doubling (ADD A) and one ADD with a saved copy (×8 + ×2), and show the result. Then do the same for 25:
LEDS ●○○○○○●○ = 130
LEDS ●●●●●○●○ = 250
hints: After one ADD A, A holds ×2: save it with MOV B,A (107).
Two more ADD A make ×8. ADD B (200) adds the ×2: ×10.
OUT 377, then the same again for 25, then HLT.

al6.title: Sum of Three
al6.story: Three measurements sit in memory, right after your program. Add them up.
al6.task:
Put the three data bytes 31, 47 and 64 right after your HLT. Use LXI H with the address of the first one, add all three with MOV A,M, INX H and ADD M, store the sum at address 200 with STA, then load it back with LDA and show it:
LEDS ●○○○●●●○ = 142

requirements.message: Point HL at the data with LXI H (041).

hints: Write the program first, then count its bytes to find where the data starts.
LXI H d: 041, address, 000. MOV A,M (176), INX H (043), ADD M (206), INX H, ADD M.
STA 200: 062 200 000. LDA 200: 072 200 000. OUT, HLT, then the three data bytes.

alc2-project.title: The Cash Register
alc2-project.story: A small shop in 1976 uses an Altair as a cash register. Three prices are in memory.
alc2-project.task:
Put the prices 12, 25 and 40 after HLT. Add them with HL and M, show the total, store it at address 200. Then work out the change from 100 (100 minus the total, with SUB) and show it:
LEDS ○●○○●●○● = 77
LEDS ○○○●○●●● = 23

requirements.message: Point HL at the prices with LXI H.
Add the prices with ADD M.
Work out the change with SUB.

hints: Total: LXI H, MOV A,M, INX H, ADD M, INX H, ADD M, OUT 377, STA 200.
Change: MOV B,A (107) to keep the total, MVI A 100, SUB B (220), OUT 377.
Count the bytes before the data for LXI H.

al7.title: Skip the Bad Byte
al7.story: Someone toggled in a byte that ruins your result. Jump over it instead of fixing the listing.
al7.task:
Your program must contain the bytes 306 and 144 (ADI 100) right after the start of the work, and jump over them with JMP. Start with MVI A 50, then the JMP, then the ADI 100, then show A and halt:
LEDS ○○●●○○●○ = 50
hints: JMP to the OUT: 303, then the OUT's address, then 000. The ADI takes 2 bytes.
The OUT is at address 007: 2 (MVI) + 3 (JMP) + 2 (ADI).

al8.title: The Bigger One
al8.story: Two sensors report their readings into memory. The panel must show the bigger one.
al8.task:
Put the bytes 73 and 91 after HLT. Load the first into B (LDA then MOV B,A), the second into A, compare with CMP B, and use a conditional jump so the lights show the bigger value:
LEDS ○●○●●○●● = 91

requirements.message: Decide with a conditional jump (JZ, JNZ, JC, JNC).

hints: LDA first (072 …), MOV B,A (107), LDA second.
CMP B (270), then JNC show: if no carry, A is the bigger one already.
Otherwise MOV A,B (170). At show: OUT 377, HLT.

al9.title: Countdown Lights
al9.story: Rocket launch at the computer club! The Altair counts down on its lights.
al9.task:
Show 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 on the lights with a loop: MVI A 5, then OUT, DCR A and JNZ back to the OUT. Then show 0 and halt:
LEDS ○○○○○●○● = 5
LEDS ○○○○○●○○ = 4
LEDS ○○○○○○●● = 3
LEDS ○○○○○○●○ = 2
LEDS ○○○○○○○● = 1
LEDS ○○○○○○○○ = 0
hints: The OUT is at address 002: jump back there.
MVI A 5, OUT 377, DCR A, JNZ 002 000.
After the loop A is 0: one more OUT 377, then HLT.

alc3-project.title: The Multiplier
alc3-project.story: The computer club wants a multiply-and-divide demo for the next meeting.
alc3-project.task:
Put 12 and 13 after HLT. Multiply them with a loop (load 12 into C, 13 into B as the counter, add C to A until B is 0) and show the product. Then divide the product by 12 by subtracting 12 while A is at least 12 (CPI 12, JC to stop), counting the rounds in D, and show the count:
LEDS ●○○●●●○○ = 156
LEDS ○○○○●●○● = 13

requirements.message: Use CPI to check if 12 still fits.
Leave the division loop with JC (or JNC).

hints: Multiply: MVI A 0, loop: ADD C, DCR B, JNZ loop, OUT 377.
Divide: MVI D 0, loop: CPI 12, JC done, SUI 12, INR D, JMP loop.
done: MOV A,D (172), OUT 377, HLT. Load 12 and 13 from memory with LDA and MOV, or LXI H and MOV C,M / MOV B,M.

al10.title: Light Switches
al10.story: The club's Altair controls 8 lamps through its lights. Switch single lamps on and off without touching the others.
al10.task:
Start with MVI A 10101010 and show it. Turn on bit 0 with ORI and show it, turn off bit 7 with ANI and show it, then flip the lower four bits with XRI and show it:
LEDS ●○●○●○●○ = 170
LEDS ●○●○●○●● = 171
LEDS ○○●○●○●● = 43
LEDS ○○●○○●○○ = 36

requirements.message: Turn a bit on with ORI (366).
Turn a bit off with ANI (346).

hints: XRI 00001111: 356 017. OUT 377 after each step.

al11.title: The Running Light
al11.story: The most famous Altair demo: a single light running across the panel.
al11.task:
Show a light running from right to left: start with A = 1, then 8 times: show A and rotate it left with RLC. Use a loop with a counter in B:
LEDS ○○○○○○○● = 1
LEDS ○○○○○○●○ = 2
LEDS ○○○○○●○○ = 4
LEDS ○○○○●○○○ = 8
LEDS ○○○●○○○○ = 16
LEDS ○○●○○○○○ = 32
LEDS ○●○○○○○○ = 64
LEDS ●○○○○○○○ = 128
hints: MVI A 1, MVI B 8.
loop: OUT 377, RLC, DCR B, JNZ loop.
Then HLT.

al12.title: Kill the Bit
al12.story: Your turn to play the famous game. The test flips the sense switches for you, one setting per round.
al12.task:
B starts at 00000001. Do 4 rounds: rotate B left (MOV A,B, RLC, MOV B,A), read the sense switches (IN 377), XOR B into them (XRA B), store the result back in B, and show it. The switches are 00000000, 00000100, 00000000 and 00000100:
LEDS ○○○○○○●○ = 2
LEDS ○○○○○○○○ = 0
LEDS ○○○○○○○○ = 0
LEDS ○○○○○●○○ = 4

requirements.message: Read the sense switches with IN 377.

hints: MVI B 1, MVI C 4 (the rounds).
round: MOV A,B, RLC, MOV B,A, IN 377, XRA B, MOV B,A, OUT 377.
DCR C, JNZ round, HLT. In round 2 the bit is killed; in round 4 a miss creates a new one.

alc4-project.title: Even or Odd
alc4-project.story: A quiz machine for the computer club: set a number on the sense switches, and the Altair tells you about it.
alc4-project.task:
Read three numbers from the sense switches. For each one, show it, then show 255 if it is odd or 0 if it is even (ANI 1 and a conditional jump), then show it halved (clear the carry, RAR). The switches are 13, 40 and 7:
LEDS ○○○○●●○● = 13
LEDS ●●●●●●●● = 255
LEDS ○○○○○●●○ = 6
LEDS ○○●○●○○○ = 40
LEDS ○○○○○○○○ = 0
LEDS ○○○●○●○○ = 20
LEDS ○○○○○●●● = 7
LEDS ●●●●●●●● = 255
LEDS ○○○○○○●● = 3
hints: Keep the number in B: IN 377, MOV B,A, OUT 377.
ANI 1, JZ even: MVI A 255 (odd) … even: XRA A. OUT 377.
MOV A,B, ANA A (clears the carry), RAR, OUT 377. Loop 3 times with C as the counter.

al13.title: Square It
al13.story: Write a routine once, call it three times.
al13.task:
Write a subroutine square that multiplies A by itself (with a loop) and returns the result in A. Call it for 5, 9 and 15 and show each result:
LEDS ○○○●●○○● = 25
LEDS ○●○●○○○● = 81
LEDS ●●●○○○○● = 225
hints: square: MOV B,A, MOV C,A, XRA A, loop: ADD C, DCR B, JNZ loop, RET.
Main: MVI A 5, CALL square, OUT 377, and the same for 9 and 15, then HLT.
15 × 15 = 225 still fits into one byte.

al14.title: The Polite Routine
al14.story: A routine that borrows registers must give them back.
al14.task:
Write a subroutine times4 that multiplies A by 4 with a loop that counts in B, but saves B (PUSH B) and restores it (POP B). The main program sets B to 77 and A to 9, calls times4, shows A, then shows B:
LEDS ○○●○○●○○ = 36
LEDS ○●○○●●○● = 77
hints: times4: PUSH B, MVI B 2, loop: ADD A, DCR B, JNZ loop, POP B, RET.
Main: MVI B 77, MVI A 9, CALL times4, OUT 377, MOV A,B, OUT 377, HLT.

al15.title: Hello, Teletype
al15.story: The Teletype is connected. Time for the first words.
al15.task: Print HELLO, ALTAIR and a line break on the Teletype with a print loop over a zero-terminated message stored after HLT (MOV A,M, ORA A, JZ, OUT 001, INX H, JMP).

requirements.message: Test for the end with ORA A (267).

hints: LXI H msg, then loop: MOV A,M, ORA A, JZ done, OUT 001, INX H, JMP loop, done: HLT.
Count the program's bytes to find the address of msg.

alc5-project.title: MEMORY SIZE?
alc5-project.story: 1975, Albuquerque. Paul Allen loads Altair BASIC from paper tape. The Teletype starts to clatter…
alc5-project.task:
Write a subroutine print (HL points to a zero-terminated message) and use it to print the opening of Altair BASIC, then show the memory size, 256, as the number of free pages on the lights (1):
MEMORY SIZE? 256
ALTAIR BASIC VERSION 1.0
OK
Then show 1 on the lights.
alc5-project.expectedOutput:
MEMORY SIZE? 256
ALTAIR BASIC VERSION 1.0
OK
LEDS ○○○○○○○● = 1
hints: Three messages after HLT, each ending with 012 (line break) and 000.
print: MOV A,M, ORA A, RZ is 310 (or JZ to a RET), OUT 001, INX H, JMP print.
Main: LXI SP 000 001, then LXI H and CALL print for each message, MVI A 1, OUT 377, HLT.
